statement: For every integer n >= 3 and every irreducible polynomial p in F_2[t] of degree n, using the associated polynomial reference basis and the complete raw Boolean extension on all matrices P (including singular P), the map f_raw(P,u) = adj(P) J_n(Pu) has algebraic degree exactly 3(n-1). This statement does not assert the unresolved equality L_ANF^joint(f_raw) = n.
contribution: An explicit uniform degree-3(n-1) ANF coefficient closes the algebraic-degree half of the frozen problem. Its coefficient is an off-diagonal entry of the inverse trace Gram matrix, and a two-path bipartite support makes the two partial-matching decomposition unique. The coefficient location may change with the irreducible reference polynomial, but the proof establishes its existence for every permitted polynomial basis. Relative to the cited 2026 v1, which proves only the matching upper bound and identifies the exact general raw values as future work, this is a nontrivial partial theorem; no global priority claim is made.
